I read the whole target file and its imported definition file, RegularisedOrderedDerivative.lean. That file defines regularisedOrderedSpatialDerivative and has no simp attributes either. I also grepped for every use of regularisedListBasisTuple. The only outside use is RegularisedInitialOrderedSobolev.lean, which applies regularisedOrderedSpatialDerivative_eq_iteratedFDeriv explicitly and rewrites with the result.

The target declares no @[simp] lemmas and no simp-set changes, so there is no wrong-direction rewrite, competing rule, unwanted expansion or cycle to report. Two things could be argued as missing simp lemmas:
- regularisedListBasisTuple_cons is only used with `rw`.
- The definition regularisedOrderedSpatialDerivative has no nil or cons unfolding lemmas, so the proofs use `change`. Those proofs are in this file and in the imported file.

Neither is supported by a use that needs it. Making the cons lemma @[simp] would put a `Fin.cons` normal form on a general tuple, which could interfere with other `Fin.cons` and `Fin.tail` simp lemmas. I could not run Lean to check that, so I did not report it. Remaining uncertainty is only about future callers I could not see.
